extractor: read from the AIMA page registered in source_roles, fetched from the VPS with the source monitor's own User-Agent
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from, verbatim and in Portuguese. Labels and descriptions are VisaAI's English and are ours, not the authority's. AIMA decides residence permits and does NOT issue visas; the MFA visa portal drops our production source address at the TCP level and is neither registered nor read, so where a route requires a residence visa we can state that it is required and not what it takes to get one.
structure_note: FOUR SALARY THRESHOLDS ON ONE ROUTE, AND THEY DO NOT ALL APPLY TO THE SAME PEOPLE. The general floor is 1.5x the national average annual gross salary (EUR 2,157.00/month) or three times the IAS. For ISCO major groups 1 and 2 professions listed as particularly in need of third-country workers, the floor drops to 1.2x (EUR 1,725.60/month) or twice the IAS (EUR 1,018.52/month). AIMA states its own reference years: 2023 for the average salary and 2024 for the IAS — so the euro figures are already two and three years old on their face, and they are recorded with those years attached rather than presented as current.
freshness_note: AIMA publishes no dateModified in its markup and no body dateline; reported as unknown, never as fresh. Where a figure carries its own reference year — the highly qualified salary thresholds do — that year is recorded with the figure.
not_extracted: Everything about obtaining the residence VISA that several of these routes require. Issued by the MFA through consular posts, published on vistos.mne.gov.pt, which resets our connection after ClientHello from the production address and answers 200 from a second egress. Not registered, not read, and the dependency is stated on each route that carries it.

The fees. Every page links a single fee schedule ('tabela de taxas e demais encargos a cobrar pelos procedimentos administrativos') rather than stating amounts, so no figure is recorded for any route.
Processing times. Not stated on any page.
How to prove means of subsistence. The pages link Portaria n.º 1563/2007 rather than stating a figure.

requirements.description: It is the general highly qualified route, and two more specific regimes take precedence where they apply.

requirements.label: Salary floor: 1.5x the national average annual gross salary (EUR 2,157.00/month) or 3x the IAS; 1.2x (EUR 1,725.60/month) or 2x the IAS (EUR 1,018.52/month) for listed ISCO group 1 and 2 professions
requirements.description: AIMA publishes the reference years itself. Recording the euro amounts without them would present two-year-old and three-year-old figures as current.
requirements.source_excerpt: em caso de trabalho subordinado – declaração da entidade patronal atestando a existência de um contrato de trabalho com vencimento mínimo correspondente a 1,5 vezes o salário anual bruto médio nacional (2.157,00 euros/mês) ou três vezes o valor indexante de apoios sociais para efeitos de emprego em profissões pertencentes aos grandes grupos 1 e 2 da classificação internacional tipo (citp), indicadas como profissões particularmente necessitadas de trabalhadores nacionais de estados terceiros, o limiar salarial previsto anteriormente deve corresponder a, pelo menos, 1,2 vezes o salário bruto médio nacional (1.725,60 euros/mês), ou duas vezes o valor do ias (1.018,52 euros/mês). os valores de referência reportam a 2023 (salário anual bruto médio) e a 2024 (ias);
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Em caso de trabalho subordinado – declaração da entidade patronal atestando a existência de um contrato de trabalho com vencimento mínimo correspondente a 1,5 vezes o salário anual bruto médio nacional (2.157,00 euros/mês) ou três vezes o valor indexante de apoios sociais Para efeitos de emprego em profissões pertencentes aos grandes grupos 1 e 2 da Classificação Internacional Tipo (CITP), indicadas como profissões particularmente necessitadas de trabalhadores nacionais de Estados terceiros, o limiar salarial previsto anteriormente deve corresponder a, pelo menos, 1,2 vezes o salário bruto médio nacional (1.725,60 euros/mês), ou duas vezes o valor do IAS (1.018,52 euros/mês). Os valores de referência reportam a 2023 (salário anual bruto médio) e a 2024 (IAS);
